name: Calendly
description: Calendly is the market-leading scheduling platform with a developer API for fetching scheduled events, managing invitees, and embedding scheduling pages. The Calendly API v2 uses OAuth2 with personal tokens for single-user apps. Widely recognized by end users — sharing a Calendly link has become a standard professional practice.

useCases.task: Embed a Calendly scheduling widget into a web app or website
Retrieve scheduled meetings and invitee data via API
Trigger actions on event scheduling via webhook
Sync Calendly bookings to a custom database or CRM

setupSteps: Create a Calendly account at calendly.com
Go to Integrations in the top-right menu
Click 'Generate New Token' under Personal Access Tokens
Copy the token and set the CALENDLY_API_TOKEN environment variable

pricing.freeTier: Free: 1 event type, unlimited scheduling, basic integrations, Calendly branding
pricing.startingPrice: $10/user/month (Standard) for unlimited event types, group events, workflows

rateLimits.limit: 1,100 requests/hour per user token; webhooks retry for 7 days on failure
rateLimits.notes: API rate limits are per access token, not per organization. Webhooks deliver real-time event notifications (invitee.created, invitee.canceled). Each webhook has a signing key for verification.
rateLimits.retryStrategy: Check X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After headers. Webhooks auto-retry with exponential backoff — return 200 immediately and process async.

sdk.importStatement: // No official SDK — use fetch or axios with the REST API

codeExamples.title: Embed Calendly scheduling widget
codeExamples.notes: Always load the Calendly widget script dynamically inside useEffect to avoid SSR hydration errors in Next.js. The widget does not support server-side rendering. Use the `prefill` option to pre-populate invitee name and email from your app's authenticated session.

codeExamples.title: Fetch scheduled events via API
codeExamples.notes: You must first call /users/me to get your user URI — all event queries require scoping to a user or organization URI. Calendly returns full URIs (not plain IDs) in all resource references. Extract the UUID from the URI tail with split('/').pop(). Use next_page_token for cursor-based pagination.

gotchas: Calendly has no official TypeScript/JavaScript SDK. The `calendly-api-v2` npm package is community-maintained and may lag behind API changes. For production use, call the REST API directly with typed interfaces.

The Calendly widget is loaded from Calendly's CDN (~200KB JS). It does NOT support SSR (server-side rendering) — always use dynamic imports or useEffect to load it client-side in Next.js/React apps to avoid hydration mismatches.
Calendly's free plan shows Calendly branding on all scheduling pages and in emails. Removing branding requires the Essentials plan ($8/month). This matters for professional or white-labeled products.

The Calendly API returns resource URIs (like https://api.calendly.com/event_types/UUID) rather than plain IDs. Extract the UUID from the URI tail using split('/').pop() — don't try to use the full URI as a database key.

reliability.notes: AWS-hosted globally. Webhook delivery retries automatically for up to 7 days on failure. Suitable for production scheduling workflows with proper async event handling.

qualityJustification: Market-leading scheduling platform with high brand recognition — users trust and know the Calendly name. Good API for syncing data. Main friction: no official SDK, free plan is heavily branded, and the widget is not SSR-compatible. Cal.com is a better choice for developers who want more control.
bestFor: Adding scheduling to apps where Calendly's brand recognition and user familiarity are assets — and for teams that need a polished out-of-the-box scheduling solution
